results.title: Why am I receiving the "RAM Memory Warning" in Playback?
results.summary: The warning appears when the iOS device is using a lot of RAM, leaving less for Playback and slowing the device. iOS steps in order: force quit background apps; save the current setlist to the Cloud, then force quit and restart Playback; clear RAM (Home-button devices: hold power 3 s until the shutdown screen, release, hold Home until the login screen; no Home button: enable AssistiveTouch under Settings > Accessibility > Touch, choose Shut Down in General, then hold the Home function in the AssistiveTouch menu until the login screen). If it continues, contact support. Mac: Playback needs at least 4 GB RAM; close all other apps including background ones (browsers, Mail, Messages), restart before service, and optionally reset PRAM (and SMC on Intel Macs only).

steps.text: iOS: force quit the other apps running in the background.
steps.caution: This stops playback for a moment; if you're live, wait for a break.

steps.text: iOS: save your current setlist to the Cloud, then force quit Playback and reopen it.
steps.caution: This stops playback for a moment; if you're live, wait for a break.

steps.text: iOS (device with a Home button): hold the power button about 3 seconds until the shutdown screen appears, release it, then hold the Home button until the login screen appears; RAM is cleared.

iOS (no Home button): turn on AssistiveTouch (Settings > Accessibility > Touch), choose Shut Down in General settings, then use the AssistiveTouch menu to hold the Home function until the login screen appears; RAM is cleared.

Mac: close all other running applications including background apps (browsers, Mail, Messages use a lot of RAM), and restart the computer before using it for service. Playback requires at least 4 GB of installed RAM.
steps.caution: This stops playback for a moment; if you're live, wait for a break.

steps.text: If the warning continues after these steps, contact MultiTracks support.

results.title: Troubleshooting Playback Download Errors
results.summary: Covers four named download error messages in Playback (Error Authorizing, Audio Files Missing, Insufficient Storage, generic Download Error) plus a catch-all. MultiTracks says download errors are rare and asks users who see the same error repeatedly to report it through the website chat. The article does not name a platform; it refers only to 'the device' and 'the Playback app'. Each step belongs to its named-error section. The remove/re-add and alternate-key quick fixes are documented under generic Download Error; that section does not establish them as Audio Files Missing recovery.

steps.text: 'Error Authorizing': the download failed a security check (your network may be blocking Playback from verifying the device). Follow the separate article 'Playback Download Error (Download Unauthorized)'.
'Audio Files Missing': tap Try Again at least three times. On the third attempt Playback runs a different recovery routine automatically.

'Audio Files Missing' (if three attempts fail on a song you recently downloaded in past setlists): open the setlist menu, scroll to the bottom, and select 'Delete All Setlists from Device'. Last resort only: it removes all local downloads and every current setlist must be downloaded again.
steps.caution: This removes the song from the device and re-downloads it, so only do it when you have time before you play.

steps.text: 'Insufficient Storage': remove past setlists with 'Delete all setlists from device' at the bottom of the setlist menu. If the error persists, check the device's storage; it may be too full. A typical song is roughly 40 MB to 1 GB, so a full setlist can be several GB.
steps.caution: This removes the song from the device and re-downloads it, so only do it when you have time before you play.

steps.text: 'Download Error' (generic): tap Try Again at least two times. If it continues and you are short on time, use Contact Support in the About tab of Playback Settings, then try the quick fixes.

'Download Error' (generic section, after retries and contacting support) - Quick fix 1 - remove and re-add the song: tap Edit, tap the red minus icon on the song, tap '+ Add Song', find the song again, and load it.
steps.caution: This removes the song from the device and re-downloads it, so only do it when you have time before you play.

steps.text: 'Download Error' (generic section, after retries and contacting support) - Quick fix 2 - download in another key and transpose locally: before loading, change the song's key in song settings to a key close to the one you need; after the download, open song settings in edit mode and change the key back.

'Download Error' (generic section, after retries and contacting support) - Quick fix 3 - clear local data (last resort): contact support first from the About tab, then open the setlist menu (top-right) and select 'Delete All Setlists from Device' at the bottom. All setlists must be redownloaded afterward.
steps.caution: This removes the song from the device and re-downloads it, so only do it when you have time before you play.

steps.text: Any other error: contact MultiTracks.com through the website messenger or 'Contact Support' in the About tab of the Playback app.

results.title: Playback | Minimum System Requirements
results.summary: Official minimums. macOS: Monterey 12.4 or later, 4 GB RAM (8 GB recommended), 1280x800, listed Mac models from 2013-2016 onward; tested fully compatible with M1 and newer. iOS/iPadOS: 15 or later, 1 GB RAM (2 GB recommended), iPhone 6s/SE 1st gen or newer, iPad 5th gen, iPad Air 2, iPad mini 4, iPad Pro 1st gen, iPod touch 7th gen. No Windows requirements are listed. Article shows 'Written by Trevor, August 4, 2026'.

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > Playback Settings > Side Menu: Settings & Features
results.text:
Playback's side menu has the following features:

- Main Settings Menu
- Waveform Size: adjustment
- Notifications: To toggle in-app notifications on or off.
- Playback Sync: To enable or disable Playback Sync broadcast from the Playback device.
- Playback Remote: The main Playback Remote menu to initiate a Playback Remote session, and/or connect a remote Playback device to a host Playback device. (📖Learn More)
- Network: the area to select which specific IP Address or network Playback Sync and Playback Remote broadcast through on host devices. (When utilizing multiple IP addresses or networks on a MacOS device).
- User Name, Organization Name, and Organization ID Number.
- Switch Organizations to switch between available organizations the signed-in user has access to.
- Log Out to log out the currently signed-in user of Playback.

Opening "Settings" in Playback's side menu will reveal the main Settings menu with the five settings' tabs; General, Tacks, Buses, MIDI, and About.

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > Playback Settings > General Settings Tab
results.text:
- Metronome Style VU: Enable the Click volume meters to flash like a metronome (enabled) or reflect the real-time volume output (disabled)
- Song Specific Master Fader: When enabled, each song has a separate master fader volume. Disable for a global master fader volume across every song.
- Fader Default Level at 80%: When enabled, a song is added to Playback with all faders preset at 80%. This provides headroom for increasing track volumes if needed. Disable to load a song with all track faders at 100% volume.
- Power Saver: Enable to improve performance on older devices and decrease battery consumption. Power Saver disables fader VU meters, Fader multi-touch, and reduces waveform scrolling feedback.
- MIDI Out: Enables the MIDI Out engine by default. Disable if not using MIDI Out; this will improve Playback performance and decrease battery consumption.
